name: cloud-account
description: Diego's Cloud Account — turns an empty phone into the owner's phone and keeps it that way: the account and its sign-in ways, the per-device profile backed up to and restored from the private vault repo, setup, and the fleet secrets (a0_docs/eng-specs/cloud-account-redesign.md). Hosts libs:account, the same code SuperApp links.

libs:autofill._doc: The non-secret autofill SOT contract (authority, permissions, columns, typed rows). Cloud Account SERVES it (AutofillSotProvider); cloud-browser and cloud-keyboard read it.

shizuku_client._doc: Cloud Account's OWN privileged shell channel (account redesign, spec section 2.4: Account is the first app on an empty phone, so it pairs first and then installs Cloud Store through pm install). Declared as Cloud Store's: the embedded wireless-adb client leads, the stock Shizuku app is the one fallback provider. SuperApp's bridge is not listed: Account must work before SuperApp exists. Read by libs/shizuku-adb-debug-tools/build.gradle (BuildConfig.SHIZUKU_CLIENT_B64).

privileged_channel._doc: What THIS app declares it needs the privileged shell channel for. Read by libs/shizuku-adb-debug-tools/build.gradle into BuildConfig.CHANNEL_NEEDS_B64 and listed, as written, in the Declared needs section of the ADB Shell page (libs:shizuku-adb-debug-tools AdbShellPage). Add a need here and it shows there; nothing about it is typed in Kotlin. Each need: id (unique), label, why (one sentence), commands (the shell verbs it runs).

shizuku_diagnostics._doc: Only the per-app local server identity. Without this block the lib falls back to the shared block whose app_process server binds 38099 (SuperApp's); Cloud Store holds 38098. Two apps on one port means the second silently fails to bind, so Account takes 38097 (free in 1_cicd/src/data/debug-ports.json, which starts at 38139 for debug APIs).

auto_update._doc_max_installs_per_pass: Most install sessions ONE unattended background pass may open. A background pass cannot show the system install dialog (Android 10+ blocks background activity starts), so each install it starts leaves a tap-to-install notification holding a PackageInstaller session until the user answers it. Unbounded, one pass over the 40-entry fleet opens 40 and the installer hits Android's 50-session cap - 'Too many active sessions for UID'. The remainder is picked up by the next pass. User-initiated 'Update all' is NOT capped: it runs in the foreground where the dialog appears and sessions resolve at once.

web._doc: #876 Cloud Account as a Kotlin/Wasm page (web/ is its own gradle root; the shared libs' pure-Compose sources arrive through the ab_cloud-libs-shared/web composite). Rendered into 1_cicd/src/cicd/ship-cloud-account-wasm.yml by the workflow generator: `./gradlew wasmJsBrowserDistribution` in `dir`, tested by test/test-account-web.sh, `build/dist/wasmJs/productionExecutable` zipped to `artifact` and attached to the rolling release as `gh_asset`. A mocked page: the island and tab strips are ui.bottom_nav / ui.sections as the Android shell reads them, the first section shows mock data and the rest say they live in the Android app. The APK's own ship ignores this directory.

unit._doc: The JVM unit suites (Robolectric): Fleet Setup, the Account vault, and the non-secret autofill SOT provider (AutofillSotProviderTest: CRUD, permission enforcement, owner-only edits, signature-level manifest). Run by the ship workflow's 'JVM unit tests' step, AFTER the JDK/SDK and the vault key are set up, through build.sh test (which resolves the shared key first; the project cannot configure without it). Scoped to :app: so a sibling library's suite cannot turn this release red.

fleet_endpoints._doc: #1093 THE fleet endpoint declaration, declared once (#1090 declared the mail part of it as mail_endpoints). Every fleet service Cloud Account talks to or shows has up to two endpoints, taken from the service's own fleet declaration in cloud-u-containers (`source`): mesh_dns / mesh_port / mesh_scheme = containers.app.dns / .port / .protocol, public_domain = proxy.domain. libs:account reads this for four things: (1) Account's own transport (libs:fleet-endpoints: mesh first with a short probe, then the public URL with the fleet bearer, cached, re-probed on a network change), (2) Connect > Status > Endpoints, (3) the `fleet_endpoints` accountdata method that publishes the pairs to the other apps, and (4) the `mail_endpoints` method, which takes the kind=mail services (Cloud Mail). A service that lives under a PATH of a shared host says public_path (and mesh_path when the mesh side differs) and route_paths (the part of it that may be routed). A service with no public_domain is mesh-only (no public route is declared, or the public name is WG-only) and must say policy mesh_only; the bearer is never declared here: it is the vault's fleet.bearer, granted per package in Secrets and sent on the exact public origin only. policy is the default: mesh_first (try the mesh, fall back to public + bearer), mesh_only, public_only. health is the path Status asks for. Every mesh endpoint is plain http (`.app` is WireGuard-only, WG encrypts) and every public URL https; each app's network_security_config.xml gets its cleartext `.app` entries GENERATED from this list (1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-android-fleet-nsc.py, data 1_cicd/src/data/fleet-nsc.json, held by FleetHostGuardTest), never hand-listed.

services._doc: The mesh endpoint is the fleet's convention: `.app` is WireGuard-only and WG already encrypts, so it is plain HTTP on the service's mesh-only port (2080 -> Stalwart's HTTP listener, bound on wg0 and wg-public like its other mesh ports; cloud-u-containers user-comm_tools-stalwart extra_ports must map it). Until that listener is shipped the mesh probe fails and Mail runs on the public URL with the bearer (the verdict is cached), so nothing breaks. The public URL stays https.

The fleet's mesh mirror of release assets (#837): the Store and the updater download through it (their own MeshMirror order). Mesh-only, declared here so its cleartext entry is generated like every other mesh host.
Only the health probe is routed: a sign-in is a browser or cookie flow bound to the auth host (Authelia refuses a session on another host name), so every other path stays on the public URL.

#1100 addressing rule: the public name is {container}.diegonmarcos.com (no api.* host, no /pub path of a shared host). mesh_path empty. route_paths is the part a direct mesh call may reach: /health, /ready and /analytics/* are the declared public_paths; the config artifact and profile connect are answered only behind the gate and stay on the public URL. The mesh leg answers once #1100 publishes the container on the mesh; until then a mesh probe fails fast and the public URL + bearer is used.

#1100 addressing rule: public {container}.diegonmarcos.com (no api.* host, no /c3-infra-api prefix). Only its declared public paths are routed over the mesh (crash and log events, public logs); the rest answers behind the gate only. The mesh leg answers once #1100 publishes the container on the mesh; until then the public URL + bearer is used.

#1100 addressing rule: public {container}.diegonmarcos.com behind the fleet bearer (no api.* host, no /news prefix); mesh news-gdelt.app:3019 (the name resolves on the mesh; the port is not published yet, so until #1100 publishes it the public URL + bearer is used). libs:news reads its default API base from this entry (BuildConfig.NEWS_API_BASE) and sends its calls over the seam. Only the read endpoints are routed.

wg_only: languagetool.diegonmarcos.com answers on the mesh alone (a remote_ip gate), so it is no second endpoint and the policy is mesh_only: the Keyboard's grammar check uses the mesh endpoint and fails as unreachable off the mesh.
No public_domain: the broker's public leg is a path under auth.diegonmarcos.com that Authelia's edge fronts, not an endpoint of its own. Its google instance (4180) stands for the broker here.
The fleet token engine behind Data > Secrets > Tokens: owner-only (the engine checks the phone's fleet bearer), wg_only like the other private services.
Mesh-only by its own declaration (deploy._host_doc: cloud-me-api.app over wg0, no public route).

vault.diegonmarcos.com is wg_only: true, so it is the name Cloud Vault's server URL carries and a second endpoint only once a bearer-protected public host exists (#1100). Until then the policy is mesh_only: a request for the name is routed onto vaultwarden.app and, with the mesh down, fails as unreachable; it is never sent to the public host. Flip the policy to mesh_first when the public host is live.

ui._doc: Cloud Account's information architecture (#1081, owner request 2026-10-21; supersedes the four islands of 2026-10-14 and #964): five sections Personal Info, Configs, Data, Connect, Activity (libs:bottomnav NavDecl), one place per thing. Configs is PUBLIC (no secret value; test-account-configs-public.sh and PublicConfigTest), Data is PRIVATE (secrets, masked by default). A page's `pages` is a second strip (NavPage.pages). MainActivity maps every leaf (section, page) to one composable; hub/HubNav.LEGACY maps every id of the earlier layouts to its place now, so libs:account links and OPEN intents (extras section/page) keep working.

account._doc: Cloud Account redesign, task 2 (a0_docs/eng-specs/cloud-account-redesign.md sections 2, 5, 6). Read by libs:account's build.gradle into BuildConfig.UI_ACCOUNT_B64 (ForgeClient.Decl). forges: where the vault lives, each written through its contents API; auth 'bearer' sends `Authorization: Bearer <t>` (GitHub), 'token' sends `Authorization: token <t>` (Gitea). A forge's token is read from AccountVault Connections at forge.<id>.token, the primary forge id at forge.primary (default: the first forge with a repo). vault: the branch, the folder the app writes per-device profiles to (devices/<id>.json, DEFAULT.json; never an emit.py input), and the generated secrets file the connect fetch keeps reading.

forges._doc_repo: null on purpose: the vault repo is NOT mirrored to Gitea (cloud-u-containers infra-dat_gitea build.json mirror_policy.exclude lists cloud-vault and cloud-me_vault), so no owner/repo path exists there. The owner declares it once a private Gitea repo for the vault exists; until then this forge is skipped (ForgeClient refuses a forge without a repo).

runbook._doc: Setup runbook (spec section 4.6): the eight step ids IN ORDER, read by libs:account SetupRunbook from BuildConfig.UI_ACCOUNT_B64. Removing an id disables that step by declaration. Implemented so far: shell (embedded adb pairing + WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS self-grant), store (install Cloud Store from the fleet release over the shell channel). The others answer TODO until their slot lands.

connect._doc: Account ▸ connect (spec 4.2): the forge ways are ui.account.forges[].ways; this adds the offline way. libs:account ConnectWays.ways() reads both and dispatches every pill on its kind (ConnectWays.handler).

perms._doc: Setup ▸ perms (spec 4.9): the shell verb table libs:account PermsPlan reads from BuildConfig.UI_ACCOUNT_B64 (nothing in Kotlin names a verb). Each verb is a template run over the uid-2000 shell channel; {pkg} {perm} {op} {component} {role} are substituted only after a strict name check. 'PackageVerifier' is not a shell line: it names the existing lib object that writes the Play Protect Settings.Global keys. needs_user: the kinds the shell cannot grant (device admin, accessibility) and the Settings action each row opens. appops: shell op name -> the AppOpsManager opstr read back and the manifest permission (or service permission) that makes an app list the row; NOTIFICATION_LISTENER is recorded with the app ops in the profile. roles: short name -> role id.
